verdict.rationale: Bitwarden explicitly documents that its browser extension autofills saved passkeys, and its integrated authenticator generates TOTP codes so users don't open a separate app and type them. However, no evidence explicitly says the extension enters TOTP codes into login fields; the general autofill doc covers only 'credentials'. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the browser extension autofilling TOTP codes into login forms, independent hands-on corroboration of passkey and TOTP autofill in the extension.

support.subject: As an everyday user, a browser extension autofills my TOTP codes and passkeys during login instead of making me retype them

citations.quote: Save passkeys in your Bitwarden vault and use the browser extension or mobile apps to autofill them across the apps and websites you use every day.

Instead of opening a separate app and manually typing codes, it automatically produces the [time-based one-time passwords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time-based_One-time_Password_algorithm) (TOTPs)
When you visit a website, the browser extension recognizes it and enters matching credentials from your vault into the login fields.
